name: Tulum
blurb: Online conversation about Tulum is currently quiet with a 24% drop in growth, as posts highlight empty storefronts and severe seaweed accumulation on beaches. However, visitors continue to share experiences ranging from cenote swimming and catamaran cruises to pre-Columbian Mayan ruins.

positive: Enjoying boat trips, cenotes, and local sunsets
Ranking high on happiness and momentum destination indices
Appreciating the culture, landscape, and friendly locals
negative: Heavy sargassum seaweed covering beaches and making them inaccessible
Numerous businesses closing down, leaving parts of the hotel zone empty
Reports of taxi drivers overcharging tourists

quotes.text: Until they left and didn’t come back. “Right now, it’s a ghost town,” says Luis Lever, a local real estate agent. Nearly half the shops in the Tulum hotel zone are now closed, according to the Tulum Times.

Enough sargassum seaweed to fill hundreds of dumpsters washes onto Tulum's idyllic beaches every day. And those who have worked there for decades say the smelly stuff compounds a crisis of government mismanagement. www.courthousenews.com/sargassum-se...

Had such a fun day exploring one of the cenotes here in Tulum 🌿 The water was amazing and it was so beautiful we ended up spending the whole day swimming and hanging out. Got some cute photos and clips too. Can't wait to share 😇
